title: Curves through prescribed points preserving a finite cover
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq2$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $T\to X$ be a
finite etale morphism with $T$ connected, and let $S\subset X(k)$ be a
nonempty finite set. There are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over
$k$ and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains
$S$, such that $T\times_X C$ is connected and $C$ is defined over a
finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$: there is an automorphism
$\varphi$ of $C$ with $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$,
where $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius
of $X$.

proof.text: Use the sections-vanishing Bertini input [lem-zl-bertini-sections] (Stacks Tag 0FD5) on a projective closure $\overline X$ of $X$ and the reduced finite closed subscheme supported on $S$. For a sufficiently large $n$, its space $V$ of sections of $\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)$ vanishing on $S$ generates the twist away from $S$ and induces an immersion on $X\setminus S$. Apply [lem-pc-serre-vanishing] to the ideal of the union of the first infinitesimal neighborhoods of the points of $S$; after increasing $n$, restriction to the direct sum of the cotangent spaces at $S$ is surjective. Thus the conditions that a section have nonzero first derivative at every point of $S$ are nonempty open conditions on $V$.

Let $s\in S$ and let $v\in V$ have nonzero image in $(\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak m_s^2)\otimes\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)|_s$ (Step 1). Since $X$ is smooth over $k$, $\mathcal O_{X,s}$ is a regular local ring [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion] (with $L=k$). In a trivialization of $\mathcal O(n)$ at $s$, $v$ is an element $f\in\mathfrak m_s\setminus\mathfrak m_s^2$, so $\mathcal O_{X,s}/(f)=\mathcal O_{H_v,s}$ is regular [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion], and $H_v\cap X$ is smooth over $k$ at the closed point $s$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-closed-point-smooth-source] ($k$ algebraically closed, applied on an affine open of $H_v\cap X$ containing $s$). The restriction $\psi:V\to\Gamma(X\setminus S,\mathcal O(n))$ generates and gives an immersion $X\setminus S\to\overline X\setminus S\to\mathbf P(V)$ (an open immersion followed by an immersion), and $X\setminus S$ is smooth, so [lem-zl-bertini-smooth-member] gives a nonempty open $U_{\rm sm}\subseteq\mathbf A(V)$ whose $k$-points cut $X\setminus S$ smoothly. Intersecting with the finitely many nonempty open derivative conditions of Step 1 gives a nonempty open whose $k$-points $v$ have $H_v\cap X$ smooth over $k$ everywhere. For such $v$, $T\times_X(H_v\cap X)$ is étale over $H_v\cap X$ (base change of $T\to X$), hence smooth over $k$; no Bertini theorem is applied to $T$ for smoothness.

Both $X$ and $T$ are smooth and connected over the algebraically closed field $k$, hence irreducible and so geometrically irreducible; $T$ has dimension $d$ since it is finite étale over $X$. Base loci: the base locus of $V$ on $X$ is $S$ (all sections vanish on $S$, and $V$ generates off $S$), and that of the pulled-back system on $T$ is the finite inverse image of $S$; finite sets of closed points have codimension $d\ge2$. Hypothesis (i) of [lem-zl-bertini-irreducible-member] on $Y\in\{X,T\}$: choose a closed point $y\in Y$ over some $x\in X\setminus S$. The morphism $Y\setminus(	ext{inverse image of }S)	o\mathbf P(V)$ is unramified at $y$ (an immersion, or an étale morphism followed by an immersion), so by [lem-sc-rational-unramified-cotangent-criterion] the cotangent space of $\mathbf P(V)$ at the image point surjects onto $\mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2$; as the former is spanned by ratios of sections of $V$ vanishing at that point, and $\dim\mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2=d\ge2$ ($\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is regular of dimension $d$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion]), there are $v_2,v_3\in V$ vanishing at $y$ with independent images in $\mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2$, and by generation some $v_1$ with $v_1(y)
eq0$. With $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $f_2,f_3$ local equations, $R/(f_2)$ and $R/(f_2,f_3)$ are regular [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] (the image of $f_3$ lies outside the square of the maximal ideal of $R/(f_2)$ by independence), hence domains [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. So $\mathfrak p=(f_2,f_3)$ is prime, exactly one irreducible component $W$ of $H_{v_2}\cap H_{v_3}$ passes through $y$, and $\operatorname{codim}(W,Y)=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p$. Now $0\subsetneq(f_2)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ is a chain of primes ($f_2
eq0$, and $f_3
otin(f_2)$ by independence), so $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p\ge2$, and $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p\le0+2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound]. Thus $\operatorname{codim}(W,Y)=2$ and $W
ot\subseteq H_{v_1}$ as $y\in W$. Hence [lem-zl-bertini-irreducible-member] gives nonempty opens of $\mathbf A(V)$ for $X$ and for $T$. Intersect them with the open of Step 2 (in the irreducible $\mathbf A(V)$) and choose a $k$-point $v$ ($k$ is infinite). Then $H_v\cap X$ and $H_v\cap T=T	imes_X(H_v\cap X)$ are smooth and geometrically irreducible, in particular connected.

The resulting closed subscheme $X_1\subset X$ contains $S$, is affine because it is closed in the affine scheme $X$, is smooth and connected, and has dimension $d-1$; its inverse image $T_1=T\times_X X_1$ is connected, finite, and etale over $X_1$. Repeat the same construction with $X_1,T_1$ and the same finite set $S$ until dimension one. At every stage the dimension is at least two when Bertini is applied, so the codimension-two base-locus hypothesis remains valid; the final $X_r$ is the required curve $C$, and connectedness of $T_r$ is the connectedness of $T\times_X C$.

proof.text: The final curve $C=X_r$ is a closed subscheme of $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ with $X_0$ of finite type over $k_0$ (smooth). By [lem-zl-bertini-finite-field-descent] applied to the closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$, there are $m\ge1$ and a closed subscheme $C_m\subseteq X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ with $C=C_m\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}k$, and an automorphism $\varphi:C\to C$ with $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma=g_X$ is the geometric Frobenius of $X$. This is the displayed Frobenius stability; smoothness, connectedness and affineness of $C$ and connectedness of $T\times_XC$ were proved over $k$ in Step 4.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq2$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $T\to X$ be a
finite etale morphism with $T$ connected, and let $S\subset X(k)$ be a
nonempty finite set. There are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over
$k$ and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains
$S$, such that $T\times_X C$ is connected and $C$ is defined over a
finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$: there is an automorphism
$\varphi$ of $C$ with $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$,
where $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius
of $X$.

proof.text:
We spell out the geometric input. We use the ordinary Bertini lemmas
[Stacks Project, Tag 0FD5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FD5)
(sections vanishing on a prescribed closed subscheme),
[Tag 0FD6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FD6)
(smoothness), and
[Tag 0G4F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G4F)
(geometric irreducibility of a linear system).
These are statements about schemes and linear systems, with no weight
or monodromy hypothesis.

Embed $X$ in projective space and let $\overline X$ be its
projective closure. For a sufficiently large $n$, let $V$ be
the space of sections of $\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)$ vanishing
on the reduced finite subscheme $S$. Tag 0FD5 makes its base locus
on $X$ exactly $S$, and makes its associated map an immersion on
$X\setminus S$. Increasing $n$ if necessary makes

$$
V\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{s\in S}
(\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak m_s^2)\otimes
\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)|_s
$$

surjective. Indeed, apply the usual eventual vanishing of coherent
$H^1$ for an ample twist to the ideal of the union of the first
infinitesimal neighborhoods of these finitely many points. Thus
nonzero first derivative at each $s$ is a nonempty open condition
on $V$. Tag 0FD6 on $X\setminus S$, together with these finitely
many derivative conditions, makes a general member smooth everywhere
on $X$.

For completeness, the hypotheses of Tag 0G4F hold both on $X$ and
for the pulled-back linear system on $T$. Both schemes are smooth
and connected over $k$, hence irreducible. The respective base
loci are $S$ and its finite inverse image, of codimension at least
two. Choose $x\in X\setminus S$. Since the linear system induces
an immersion there, choose two sections vanishing at $x$ with
independent differentials, and a third section nonzero at $x$.
The common zero locus of the first two has a codimension-two component
through $x$ not contained in the third divisor. At any point of
$T$ above $x$, etaleness gives the same assertion for the
pulled-back sections. These verify the remaining hypothesis of
Tag 0G4F. A general member therefore cuts both $X$ and $T$
in irreducible subschemes. Intersect the finitely many nonempty open
conditions on the irreducible parameter space $V$, and choose a
$k$-point in their intersection.

The resulting $X_1$ is a smooth connected closed affine subscheme
of dimension $d-1$, contains $S$, and its inverse image $T_1$
is connected and finite etale over it. Repeat this construction until
dimension one. In dimension two the same argument applies, since
the finite base locus still has codimension two. This proves the
claim about $C$. Over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ all the finitely
many defining equations and morphisms involve only finitely many
coefficients, so descend to one finite constant-field extension.
Geometric smoothness and connectedness are the properties just proved
after base change to $k$.

split_report.summary: Updated the imported statement to the current main-20261015 finite-field geometric-fiber formulation and split the proof into the three Stacks Bertini inputs, the dimension-reduction iteration, and finite-constant-field descent. The only matching slopmaster2 declaration is sorry-backed, so it is not an attachment. Maintainer reader (cc review) repaired steps 2, 3 and 5: cited the regularity and cotangent tools for the derivative conditions and the codimension-two component, removed the Bertini application to T for smoothness (T-cut is étale over the X-cut), and applied the corrected closed-subscheme descent node directly to C.
split_report.blueprint: Steps realize the main-20261015 proof paragraphs 2 (Tag 0FD5 and derivative conditions), 2 (Tag 0FD6), 3 (Tag 0G4F), and 4 (iteration and finite-field descent).

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses eventual vanishing for the ideal of the first infinitesimal neighborhoods to obtain surjectivity of first derivatives; this is a generic coherent-cohomology input absent from the Bertini unit's own nodes.
Steps 2-3 take regularity of the local rings of the smooth k-schemes X and T (case L=k); a generic commutative-algebra tool, no node of the Bertini unit states it.
Steps 2-3 take Stacks 00NQ (R/f regular for f in m minus m^2) to turn the first-derivative conditions into regularity; generic tool.
Step 2 takes regular-at-a-closed-point implies smooth over the algebraically closed field k at the points of S; generic tool.
Step 3 takes surjectivity on cotangent spaces for the unramified map to P(V) to find v2,v3 with independent differentials; generic tool.
Step 3 takes that regular local rings are domains, so (f2) and (f2,f3) are prime; generic tool.
Step 3 takes Krull height bound ht P <= ht(P/J)+t to get codim(W)<=2 as required by Tag 0G4F; generic tool (Mathlib leaf).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q137-7a71e23f0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes, every cited statement, and the sources: blueprint main-20261015 (the item statement is verbatim the current blueprint, so the update is not a weakening) and the local Stacks text of 0FD5 (varieties.tex l.10821), Situation 0FD3/0FD6 (l.10910-10964) and 0G4F (more-morphisms.tex l.9055). No SGA source is used, and the slopmaster2 declaration has a sorry, so it was correctly not attached. Steps 1 and 4 are correct as written: 0FD5 applies on the projective closure, Serre vanishing (0B5U) for the ideal of the points' first-order neighbourhoods gives surjectivity onto the cotangent spaces, and the iteration keeps the cut affine, smooth and connected with base locus S of codimension at least 2. I repaired three faults in fixes/. (a) Delivery errors B2/B4/E2 in lem-zl-bertini-finite-field-descent: X_0 was never introduced, a $ was unclosed, and the data clause was not a precise statement; with X_0 arbitrary it is false (the disjoint union of A^1's over all n, taking one point of degree n in the n-th copy, has no m). I restated it for X_0 of finite type and a closed immersion C into X_0 x k, and checked that version: finitely many coefficients, gluing by faithful flatness, and gamma^m fixes F_{q^m}. Step 5 now applies it directly to C. (b) B2/B7/B4 in the 0FD6 and 0G4F nodes: 'general' was never defined, 'linear system' was vague, and one $ was unclosed. I rewrote both in the terms of Situation 0FD3 (psi, H_v=Z(psi(v)), Zariski open of A^r, all k'-points) with the hypotheses checked one by one against the source. I also added stmt_deps to the 0FD5 node. (c) C1/E1 in steps 2-3: the steps turned 'nonzero derivative' into 'smooth', and claimed sections with independent differentials and a component of codimension exactly 2, with nothing cited; they also implied applying 0FD6 on T, where the map is not an immersion. Repaired with existing nodes: geometric-regularity-smooth criterion, 00NQ hypersurface criterion, regular closed point over an algebraically closed field is smooth, unramified cotangent criterion, regular local rings are domains, and the Krull height bound (giving height exactly 2). Smoothness on T now comes from the cut on T being etale over the cut on X. I accepted these as tool uses, together with lem-pc-serre-vanishing. No duplicates: rg for bertini, descent and spreading-out over the DAG found only nodes with different statements. Edge cases checked: d=2, a single point in S, the trivial cover.
